title: Degen Coin Flip Degen Spin exploit
lossDescription: Operator-reported ~$10,000 house loss. No independent reconstruction is published. The 30,000+ wallet figure is the project's count of participating addresses, not distinct attackers or stolen player balances.
summary: On 6 Nov 2026 Degen Coin Flip, a Solana on-chain casino that has players bet from their own wallets, disclosed an exploit in its Degen Spin game. The project said more than 30,000 wallets took part and that damage was limited to about $10,000, all from the house. Player funds were described as safe because the project does not custody balances. Spin and side bets were paused; other games were said to be unaffected. SlowMist lists the event as a smart-contract vulnerability. The project has not published the vulnerable logic, whether the bug is on-chain or off-chain, a full attack window, or a verified fixed deployment.
details: Official disclosure was posted at about 2026-11-06T04:04Z. A follow-up at 04:29Z named funding wallet 8JUEoHNMbWM4eegcMvx6ZQJt3V3fbo8JNjpWiCtJgxfF (Solscan Coinbase Hot Wallet label), collecting wallet 6LPotyCnDBy1uRu5F4CMoKhT7sMCS2mfFCo68cw9jFPi, and October 28 funding transaction NLgKpp9JqYGDz2mxw6Ruu8c2KKgXeAFB2p27JVGb4gx3YFk6dhaubkJYJEG3zVoaCycu3k3oDKSg7j9ebHQzmGP. That funding date does not establish when exploitation began, and a Coinbase-labelled shared hot wallet is not an attacker-only indicator. A ~$10,000 house loss across tens of thousands of wallets is consistent with a small per-round edge being taken many times, not with a treasury drain. This entry does not treat other Degen Coin Flip games as verified-safe beyond the project's statement.
rootCause: Unpublished. SlowMist classifies it as a smart-contract vulnerability. The operator confirmed an exploited game flaw in Degen Spin and did not describe the instruction, account, or off-chain path. This entry does not infer a specific bug class.
response: Degen Coin Flip paused Degen Spin and side bets while working on a fix and said other games remained up. No hashed patch, program upgrade, or make-whole transaction is included here. Reopening is a promise, not a verified remediation.

sources.label: SlowMist Hacked DB — Degen Coin Flip

lesson: An on-chain game that does not custody player balances can still lose the house pot: isolate each game's bankroll, cap per-wallet and per-block payouts, and do not treat a pause of one game as proof that sibling games share no code.
mitigations: Cap per-wallet and per-block payouts from the house pot so tens of thousands of automated wallets cannot grind a small edge into a material drain before pause.
Isolate each game's bankroll and program path; a pause of Degen Spin must not assume Crash, coin-flip, or blackjack share no vulnerable instruction.
Rate-limit new wallets and identical bet patterns against a single game; 30,000 wallets is an automation signal, not 30,000 independent players.
Publish the vulnerable instruction, program ID, and a verified fixed deployment before reopening; a pause plus a promise is not a patch.
Keep the house pot sized to worst-case automated extraction during the detection window, not to marketing TVL.
Do not treat a Coinbase-labelled funding wallet as attacker infrastructure; shared exchange hot wallets fund many users.

title: Loopscale Genesis Vault exploits
lossDescription: Two separate drains of Loopscale Genesis vaults, not one bug. Vector 1 (2026-11-01): 4,597 SOL left the SOL Genesis vault (wSOL ATA 5,719.566856263 → 1,122.566856263) and was extracted as 4,596 SOL plus 1.677556797 SOL, then Relay-bridged to ~190.22 ETH. Vector 2 (2026-11-05): 586,000 USDC withdrawn against 65,000 USDC deposited (net 521,120 USDC). SOL make-whole of +4,598.434180621 wSOL is hashed on 2026-11-03. No inbound USDC to the vault token account was visible at a ~2026-11-05T23:00Z check. This entry does not convert SOL to USD. An attached reconstruction combined the two vectors at ~$950k (pointer, not independently recomputed). Loopscale later cited ~$412k and ~$521k (reported).
summary: On 1 Nov and 5 Nov 2026 two distinct attacks hit Loopscale Genesis vaults on program 1oopBoJG58DgkUVKkEzKgyG9dvRmpgeEm1AVjoHkF78. They are not the April 2025 RateX oracle incident and they are not collapsed into one bug here. Vector 1 (SOL vault, 2026-11-01T19:41:05Z, slot 464213236): signer 247Lk5YNH9URfBBvxVUtDruz8GvGX8gKGuYHVCZThpiR plus Loopscale co-signer CyNKPfqsSLAejjZtEeNG3pR4SkPhSPHXdGhuNTyudrNs ran CreateLoan, DepositCollateral, UpdateWeightMatrix, and BorrowPrincipal in mZCoHzevv7nrPsSJDjnGZVRQMeUvuwQ2BuPUeCWhCYBheaWjoRkETU6Jh6zb2o2bgrhRAA4axy2QNQtpDZNFsmD. One kySOL (9 decimals), bought for 1.310991880 SOL at 19:38:31Z, was valued using a zBTC (8 decimals) identity. Vault wSOL fell 4,597 SOL (5,719.566856263 → 1,122.566856263). The drain signer is 247Lk, not AzPh. Vector 2 (USDC vault, 2026-11-05): AzPh2dUV3duK9n8PWV6CxKMwWr9Rk7fxPNBZuv1CjwMr created its own strategy, borrowed 120 USDC against 2 wSOL, deposited 65,000 USDC for 58,326.202736 shares, set a strategy rate field to 0xfffffffffffffffe, refinanced and sold the ledger to the vault for 120.000071 USDC, then burned 465.264135 shares for 586,000 USDC at 06:09:33Z. Loopscale’s published attacker list used AzPh…CiwMr, which has no history; the real signer is …CjwMr. A Squads-gated program upgrade at 2026-11-04T04:52:42Z preceded vector 2; no later program-data upgrade was seen through ~23:00Z Nov 5. That check does not claim the program is unpatched today. SOL make-whole is hashed on 2026-11-03; no USDC make-whole was visible on the vault token account at the Nov 5 check. Loopscale stated that affected vaults were made whole and no user deposits incurred a loss; that claim is sourced and is not treated as false, and it is contrasted with the limited on-chain observation.
details: Both attack wallets were funded from seed 2ByCbD4ZdwPH19DaHa6gqaMZoqUCvg84BRVFPWxJtMvw (FixedFloat-labelled 5ndLnEYqSFiA5yUFHo6LVZ1eWc6Rhh11K5CfJNkoHEPs and unlabeled A1safaZVY24vCompd8jFBq9k2Apu6SiBDh3xJ4DqAAGV on 2026-10-29). Co-signer CyNKPfqsSLAejjZtEeNG3pR4SkPhSPHXdGhuNTyudrNs is on every attacker Loopscale instruction in this reconstruction. Chain does not show that key was stolen and this entry does not assert it. Address-poisoning lookalikes (including AC9Y7HPSSmPouNBLo1cHTVbZoYRPZyUeVbBPSGt9jwMr) are noise, not attacker receipts. No on-chain link to Binance Oct 29 wallets was found. Admin signer bs1PuRvB9rBBZkryBjADYvxc2qYh51EVW2fsb1uTiBN posted CreateTimelock transactions after vector 2; payload semantics are not decoded here and this entry does not assert a pause from those hashes. Unresolved EVM destinations stay unresolved.
rootCause: Two separate causes. Vector 1 (reported by r0bre, not independently binary-diffed here): an oracle_type==19 / BeamAccount early return in verify_collateral_data skipped the asset-type check, so an Orca label could be applied with the wrong mint and price identity. The exploitable on-chain effect was a 9-decimal kySOL amount valued as 8-decimal zBTC. r0bre reports the bug was introduced in the 2026-03-18T19:11:34Z upgrade and removed in the 2026-11-04T04:52:42Z upgrade. Vector 2 (inference, medium-high confidence, not an official root cause): an uncapped strategy rate field (0xfffffffffffffffe) inflated vault book value so a small LP-share burn redeemed 586,000 USDC. Loopscale’s 2026-11-06 statement described selling a loan with an extreme interest rate into the USDC Genesis Vault and inflating NAV; that is reported, not independently confirmed as the same mechanism. The Nov 4 patch is not treated as a fix for vector 2.
response: SOL Genesis vault: LiquidateLedger by rektbdF5r7HnWrPDRvD76pC1V9rVfaGmbSY3Dsrj8Kx at 2026-11-03T13:43:50Z (47zp5i14ERm2soQQGLs5LKRk4Xi2Yigh6iuJ68URKe4VfzC9u2GpgWYbLG73fT4a645GBnUibZ5gP69kfaD7DbAo) credited +4,598.434180621 wSOL to vault ATA 8oCX3kkgviLPxYGBfSt1kCKWVmHer1pHqutPTiBYnGpu and +1 kySOL to the liquidator. That Loopscale operated the liquidator is inference. Program 1oopBoJG… was upgraded at 2026-11-04T04:52:42Z (HSuUTAA2qqzDLm5q5oKYNwjzxqpWaTKXP1XYCrSis5FkNqvDJHsU5542YsaoZJU2MGsk9jTs8FkkPWjddt4wYYi); r0bre reports that upgrade removed the type-19 early return. Vector 2 still executed after that upgrade. USDC vault token account 3GAu8zG1bLHEd2K5JUvysEjLSkfTw4aXYCFaUcQCYsA2 showed zero inbound USDC after 06:09:33Z and balance 1,638,608.740128 USDC at ~23:00Z Nov 5, so no USDC make-whole was visible on-chain at that check. Loopscale (X, 2026-11-05T10:13:27Z, 2118285556123611378) said affected vaults had been made whole and no user deposits incurred a loss, and that it paused protocol activity; pause is Loopscale’s claim, not a decoded on-chain instruction. Off-chain mitigation via the co-signer cannot be inferred. This write-up does not claim vector 2 remains unpatched after the Nov 5 check.

lesson: A lending vault can be hit twice in one week by two unrelated accounting bugs. An oracle-type exception that skips asset-type checks turns a decimal mismatch into a drain, and an uncapped strategy-rate field can inflate vault NAV after a patch that only closed the first path. A mandatory co-signer is not an independent control if it will sign whatever the program would accept.
mitigations: Require collateral mint, price identity, decimals, and asset type to be consistent; do not early-return on special oracle types such as BeamAccount before that check.
Cap strategy interest-rate fields and reject near-u64::MAX rates before refinance or sell-to-vault.
Make the backend co-signer validate mint vs price identity vs decimals independently of on-chain acceptance.
After any vault exploit, inventory remaining share-pricing and strategy-accounting paths before treating a program upgrade as complete.
Bound vault share redemption so a tiny LP-share burn cannot withdraw a disproportionate fraction of vault cash.
Publish make-whole hashes against the same token account that was drained so a depositor-whole claim can be reconciled on-chain.
Treat lookalike addresses as address-poisoning noise until a spend from a known attacker key is hashed.

lesson: A hot-wallet signer that will sign a bare System transfer is a withdrawal-pipeline bypass. Policy has to sit at the signer (shape, destination, amount), not only in the builder that produces durable-nonce withdrawals. Chain cannot distinguish a compromised signing service from a leaked key.
mitigations: Reject any hot-wallet signature that is not the normal withdrawal shape (durable nonce plus compute-budget instructions plus expected transfer).
Enforce destination allowlists and amount/velocity caps at the signing service, independent of the withdrawal builder.
Alert and auto-pause when an outflow lacks a durable nonce or exceeds size thresholds.
Isolate the signing service from the withdrawal-service container so a compromised DevOps laptop cannot submit arbitrary payloads.
Rotate the hot-wallet key after any unauthorized signed outflow; treat "no key leak" as unproven until a post-mortem.

Enforce per-transaction policy at the signer: destination allowlists, spend caps, and delays, so RCE or key access cannot drain wallets in 94 seconds.
Alert on mass simultaneous System transfers from operator-issued wallets and halt signing within minutes.
Treat a drained hot wallet as burned; refund to new user-controlled addresses, not the drained keys.

title: Blockdaemon / Solflare validator operator-key compromise
lossDescription: Bitquery recounts 1,343 SOL-worth (~$135K), 62% of it JitoSOL from identity keys, bridged to Ethereum and 57.0 ETH deposited into Tornado Cash. First public counts that stated only the SOL figure were low. Delegated stake was not taken. Solflare had about 1.56M SOL delegated to the affected validator when rewards stopped; that principal stayed in users' own stake accounts. This entry uses Bitquery's $135K operational-fund figure.
summary: On 26–27 Oct 2026 operator keys for a small set of long-running Solana validators were used to empty identity and vote accounts and to change vote-account withdraw authorities. Bitquery traces one attacker holding keys of five validators (Solflare's, Blockdaemon's, Astraeus, J21SMP, and an inactive Slow Ventures validator), taking about 1,343 SOL-worth (~$135K) in minutes, then bridging to Ethereum and depositing 57 ETH into Tornado Cash. Delegated SOL was never moved: stake accounts are controlled by the delegator's own authorities. Affected validators missed the Validator Admission Ticket and stopped earning from epoch 1070. Blockdaemon's 5 Nov 2026 update (Foresite and Mandiant) says the 2020–2022 key material was copied from a former employee's corporate device to systems outside Blockdaemon during that person's December 2025 off-boarding, not from a breach of current validator hosts. Solflare pledged to cover missed rewards for users who migrate to a replacement validator.
details: Bitquery: just after 19:00 UTC on 26 Oct, identity keys of Solflare, J21SMP, Blockdaemon and Astraeus paid a brand-new wallet 9LsvNgeMJwzC5WZ7QDzYo7wVykZmGsPBRPKtXt3a5Qr8 (~1,188 SOL-worth in 3 minutes); vote accounts were emptied before the 20:58 UTC epoch check that picks the next voting set. Keys of one validator paid fees for thefts from another, so one holder signed for all five. Withdraw authorities were moved to 6sSJnc… on 27 Oct, then to five fresh keys on 28 Oct; those new keys have done nothing else, so on-chain control is not shown as returned. A 1 SOL rescue into Solflare's empty vote account was taken 5 seconds later. Bridgers and Chainflip paid Ethereum 0x9bdde8b8f610217132cd18f29864167142ee4581; 57.0 ETH went into Tornado Cash. The same Bridgers→Ethereum route was tested 11 days earlier. Blockdaemon's 5 Nov update also names one internal operational wallet besides the five validators. No unauthorized activity after 2026-10-27T10:29Z; replacement vote account 9ntyW2ufs5hGECKLwhR4p7PuQhqAbfKdAwNoYbgXsExn. Solflare did not name the provider in its first posts; Blockdaemon later published the operator-key incident report.
rootCause: Blockdaemon (5 Nov 2026, with Foresite and Mandiant): affected credentials were generated 2020–2022; a copy sat on a former employee's corporate device and was copied to systems outside Blockdaemon during that person's off-boarding in December 2025. The unauthorized copy was not detected at the time. Validators created in 2024 or later use a different, unaffected key-generation process. Independent review found no intrusion on current validator hosts and no unauthorized access in secrets-management or password vaults from Oct 2025 through the incident. Bitquery's on-chain record is consistent with copied identity and withdraw keys, not a protocol bug. The identity of the unauthorized party has not been determined.
response: Blockdaemon opened an incident on 27 Oct, told customers to deactivate and re-delegate, rotated withdraw authority on unaffected Solana validators, and published replacement vote account 9ntyW2ufs5hGECKLwhR4p7PuQhqAbfKdAwNoYbgXsExn. The 5 Nov update says the incident is contained: the five affected vote accounts and identity accounts have been permanently retired, replacement validators are live, and withdraw authorities on every other Blockdaemon Solana mainnet validator have been rotated. Solflare said user funds were untouched, moved users toward a new validator, and pledged missed-reward compensation for those who migrate in-app. CoinDesk (29 Oct) and Solana Compass warned not to stake with the old Solflare validator. No hashed recovery of the stolen operational funds is included here.

sources.label: Parameter — Solflare bunker mode / migration window

lesson: Validator identity keys and vote withdraw authorities are hot operational secrets: a leftover 2020–2022 copy on a departed employee's laptop is enough to empty vote accounts, steal identity-held JitoSOL, change commission, and knock the validator out of the admission set, while stakers' principal stays safe only because the protocol keeps stake authorities separate.
mitigations: Keep vote-account withdraw authority on an offline / hardware-backed key that never lives on the validator host or in a former employee's laptop image; rotate it on every offboarding.
Do not park JitoSOL or other treasury on the identity (hot) key; that account should hold only fees needed to vote.
Inventory every historical validator key from discontinued generation practices and treat an unaccounted copy as already compromised.
Monitor identity and vote-account outflows and withdraw-authority changes; auto-alert when several validators share a fee payer on those txs.
Publish replacement vote-account addresses only on a canonical page; lookalike validator addresses circulated during this incident.
Tell delegators immediately that the old validator cannot earn, and that topping up a compromised vote account just feeds the attacker who still holds withdraw authority.

Do not honor destination-chain ReleaseToken / equivalent claims unless source-side fee settlement is verified, not only a claim signature.
Monitor destination vault outflows that are unmatched to paid source withdrawals and pause release programs on divergence.
Treat Arkham/Etherscan/Blockscout labels (including HitBTC) as attribution only until a chain-native label or hashed deposit proof exists.

This is product/ops custodial key exposure with multi-user fund loss, not a protocol exploit and not one-off phishing: every drain is an ordinary system transfer signed by the victim wallet, with no approval and no drainer program. Candy generated and held the keys. How those keys left Candy's custody is unpublished. At 23:58:22 UTC on 12 Oct, slot 456235850, signature 3giXDYdxn9QrfNV5gB7URkgRZCmCroPof7E9ZDmXvP82sq9WChZBXzVkwKf77bZFYuabQhBKndSEwiebkzCYcT6r, the collector sent 420 SOL to FvNJKwKcVJahVCbKE6JFuic59FRWGqZBt3xgeVp9TFcz. rootCause: Unconfirmed. Candy generated and held the keys for users' Phantom-based wallets, so the on-chain pattern looks like a bulk key leak. This entry does not infer how those keys left Candy's custody.
response: Candy's 12 Oct 2026 community update said it initiated a security protocol that locks minted NFTs (no transfers or sales between wallets) until the platform and user control can be reestablished; two internal audits had given Candy no reason to believe NFTs were lost. Candy said it was preparing to reimburse customers for drained Solana and to communicate platform-reboot plans. Public reports place the lockdown announcement at 00:22 UTC on 12 Oct 2026, between the two drain waves. Reimbursement is an official promise and is not hashed here.
lesson: A marketplace that generates and holds keys for users' wallets is a custodian: once those keys are exposed, many user wallets can be emptied with ordinary signed transfers, and locking the website or NFT transfers does not revoke copies of the keys.
mitigations: Avoid custodial private-key models; use session keys, MPC, or non-custodial signing so the operator never holds a full user key.
If keys must be held, store them in HSM/KMS with per-user envelopes; never expose raw key material to operators, logs, or export paths.
Monitor for mass simultaneous transfers from operator-issued wallets and circuit-break signing plus warn users within minutes.
Tell users that a drained hot wallet is burned; do not send new funds to an old operator-issued address.
Publish which products and address cohorts were in scope, and rotate users onto new keys before the next sweep window.
Treat a website or NFT-transfer lock as containment of remaining inventory, not as key revocation.
